A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Generator Matching research, retaining the core framework, propositions and image experiments. Their full texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image and protein generation experiments in Section 9, Tables 2–3, and checkerboard simulations in Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 reports image and protein experiments, expanded checkerboard analyses in Appendix E, and original CIFAR-10 loss-function experiments in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The general GM recipe remains, but its concrete models expand substantially. Section 9 replaces the FrameFlow-based structure model with a MultiFlow-based joint structure–sequence model. Appendix E introduces a mixture-path flow and a three-component superposition; Appendix I implements cosh- and exponential-based Bregman training losses.

E1.justification: Protein evaluation expands from structure generation to joint structure–sequence generation, alongside a retained structure-only task. This directly tests multimodal generation. CIFAR-10, ImageNet32 and the checkerboard distribution were already evaluated in v1; their additional analyses do not constitute new datasets.

E2.justification: The protein comparison changes from FrameDiff and FrameFlow to FrameFlow, RFdiffusion, FoldFlow, Protpardelle, ProteinGenerator and MultiFlow; FrameDiff disappears from the reported comparison. The expanded checkerboard comparison also adds flow under the mixture path. The image benchmark comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix G.4 changes protein evaluation from 690 samples across lengths 60–128 to 400 samples at lengths 70, 100, 200 and 300, and changes rotation discretization from 1024 to 2056 bins. V2 adds designability reporting and separate multimodal/unimodal comparisons. New experiments introduce 5–500 NFE sweeps and flow-only loss comparisons using dopri5. Protein sampling remains at 100 steps.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's trajectory illustrations and image-sampler comparison, Appendix E systematically examines probability-path/process combinations and sensitivity to sampling NFEs, including mixture-path flow failures. Appendix I adds CIFAR-10 ablations of Bregman loss choices and their training dynamics. These substantially expand analysis of design choices and numerical sensitivity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional generated-sample counts and training curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Image FIDs are unchanged between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2. The protein results are replaced under different models and protocols, with new multimodal and designability entries; v2 reports multimodal diversity of 0.48 for jumps versus 0.38 for MultiFlow. Appendix I newly reports flow-only FID 2.62 for MSE versus 2.54 for a modified Bregman loss. These are new comparisons, not direct v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal strong/weak time-reversal definitions and a general KFE criterion in Appendix A.4. Appendix E adds several path-specific derivations and an impossibility argument for a zero-drift diffusion generating the CondOT path. It also restores missing B-function terms in the Bregman sufficiency proof. These changes extend mathematical substance beyond the retained core propositions and revised notation.

C1.justification: The central unification, generator characterization, Bregman training and model-combination claims remain. The introduction's experimental contribution changes from protein structure generation to multimodal protein generation, while Section 9 replaces FrameFlow-focused improvement claims with state-of-the-art claims for MultiFlow jump variants. This expands the empirical claim without redefining the framework.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive interpretations connecting transport versus jumps to probability-path suitability and explaining discretization sensitivity through large Lipschitz constants and repeated small movements. Appendix A further explains the regularity restrictions and why matching marginals can suffice without full time reversal. Appendix I interprets alternative losses as improving training stability.

D1.justification: Appendix G.4 changes the implementation/checkpoint source from FrameFlow to MultiFlow and newly specifies model size, NFE usage and reliance on default configurations. Appendix I documents loss-mixture weights and its sampler. Most image implementation details remain in Appendix F, although the explicit joint-model output-channel count is omitted from the revised main text.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against prior jump-based generation through a new Appendix H.7 covering piecewise-deterministic models, Lévy-process models and trans-dimensional jump diffusion. It also adds a substantive Blackout Diffusion discussion and citations supporting new theoretical and protein comparisons. MultiFlow was already discussed in v1; its empirical comparator role is new.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose remain. V2 standardizes capitalization and measure notation, clarifies explanations, reorders image/protein experiments, reorganizes Appendix E and removes the acknowledgments. Much of the appendix expansion comprises new scientific content rather than rewriting existing exposition.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the protein montage, expands the protein comparison into multimodal/unimodal columns, and adds the systematic model table, full protein table, checkerboard comparison/NFE panels and loss-training plot. Some checkerboard displays expand existing Figure 2 material. The original manifold illustration is retained as Figure 9 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the framework's distinctive multimodal and loss-flexibility claims through actual co-design experiments and loss ablations. Its systematic path/process study explains practical failure conditions, while expanded prior-work discussion improves positioning. The gains concern evidential and explanatory quality, not comparable cross-version score improvements. Limitations remain: uncertainty is unreported, and Table 5 shows lower designability for jump variants despite higher diversity, making the blanket claim of best results in all categories too strong.
